key_insight: The paper introduces a "living" benchmark that can automatically generate evaluation question-answer pairs for information retrieval from electronic health records, making clinical AI testing easier to scale and update. This helps keep benchmarks aligned with rapidly changing EHR systems and LLM-based assistants.
problem_solved: Existing EHR retrieval benchmarks are expensive to manually curate, difficult to maintain, and quickly become outdated as medical records, workflows, and AI capabilities evolve.
method: Automatically generates question-answer pairs from electronic health record data.
Uses a scalable framework designed to refresh the benchmark over time instead of relying on static, manually curated test sets.
Supports evaluation of LLM-based clinical assistants on realistic information-retrieval tasks from patient records.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more practical and sustainable way to test clinical retrieval systems at scale. It can improve benchmark freshness, reduce labeling cost, and make comparisons between models more reliable in fast-moving healthcare settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing EHR data flowing into automated QA generation and benchmark updates.
Before-vs-after comparison of static manual benchmarks versus a living benchmark.
Icon set for EHR, LLM assistant, and evaluation metrics.
Chart showing benchmark freshness or maintenance cost over time.
paper_title: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records
paper_authors: Jordan L. Cahoon, Chloe O. Stanwyck, Sulaiman Somani, Philip Chung, Kevin R Keet
